content.rationale:
Both endpoints are code: xulmunov's artifact is the flat module `src/verb_draft.rs` whose handler has the dispatcher's shape (ynvwvzrm), and the check is a runnable test, the code-to-code cell. The crate is self-contained per knqkxzns and flat per szmuyqrq: `tests/verb_draft/src/lib.rs` includes `src/verb_draft.rs` and the modules it may call through `#[path]` shims at the crate-root names they have in the binary, so the handler is exercised exactly as `Verb` dispatches it. It runs the handler over scratch repositories made with `jj git init` in the system temp directory, with real change ids naming the node documents, and observes the call only through the files, directories and jj state it leaves; nothing touches the round's own repositories.

The surface use (szvotxpq, vnwmpwrx). A call naming two nodes opens two drafts: the test reads exactly two `.deccy/work/<handle>.json` documents, each record keyed by the filename's handle and written `open`, naming one node, one edit and the workspace by name and path, and finds two new jj workspaces whose listed roots are the records' paths. The lines returned are one per draft, each naming its handle and its path, in the order the nodes were named. A node named twice yields two records, two distinct handles and two distinct paths. The record is not a node document: it is read at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, and `nodes/` is byte-for-byte unchanged after the call.

The refusal use (xzrkrmmr) and the argument surface (qtqnuqxo). A call naming no node, with and without `--edit`, comes back as an `Err` refusal carrying a cause, with no record and no workspace written; an argument the form does not name refuses naming it; and `--help` answers on a context with no repository, before any store is taken, with one line naming the verb (xlvoxmyl, rwlywqrk). The refusal is a value carrying its cause and evidence (popowxnw), and the handler returns its lines rather than writing them (utrzvyyt).

The record use (kwqnrzoz, owyntkvw, vkkwusty, zsvukpls). Each record is keyed by a handle that is its filename, carries exactly one node, one edit and one workspace, is the one JSON document its handle names, and is written `open`; its base has one entry for every path of the node's owned set — here the inline node document alone — each a non-empty content identity (zsvukpls). `--edit` is carried into the edit reference, and an omitted flag falls back to the edit the invocation is made in. Opening writes no operation marker: `.deccy/markers.json` is left absent, so undo and redo receive no unit of their own (ooquotol).

The workspace use (xqzstoyo, lpkssxpp, qxuzyvsr, tyoypkmp, pvnszwum). Each record's workspace is an absolute working-copy directory outside the repository, its last path component the record's handle, listed by jj under the name the record carries at exactly that root; two repositories' drafts sit under different namespaces of one per-user root. The record is written last: with the repository's namespace made unwritable, the open refuses and no record is written (qxuzyvsr). The workspace addition is read through the `Jj` seam the implementation owns (tyoypkmp), not bypassed by the test.

The start-revision use (pvnszwum, tyoypkmp). The verb creates the draft's workspace at the change that owns the named node, so the working copy holds the node's owned set as the record's base records it. The check opens a draft for a node whose owned set is a real file: the node document lists `src/lib.rs` in its `content.ref`, and the node's change holds `src/lib.rs` with one content while a later change, the parent of the invocation's edit, holds another. A second graph is flat, the node's change followed by `jj new zzzzzzzz` so the invocation's parent is the empty root, and the draft is opened there as well. In both graphs the test reads the workspace the record names and requires every path of the record's base to hold, in the working copy, content whose `draft_identity::identity` equals that path's base entry, and requires `src/lib.rs` to be the node's content rather than the later change's. The revision is exercised through the verb's call into the workspace seam, not by calling `add` directly: what is checked is that opening a draft starts its working copy at the node's change (pvnszwum), by whatever argument the implementation carries it. Two further shapes read the same start: an explicit `--edit` naming a later change does not become the workspace's start, so a draft opened with `--edit` on a change whose `src/lib.rs` differs still holds the node's owned content (and the record carries that edit, so the start and the edit are distinguished); and two nodes named in one call each start at their own change even when the invocation's working copy is an empty change on the root holding neither owned file, so the second and later drafts are not opened at `@`.

The building blocks (ttkuyvxp, upuuwzmr, rroqqrzq, tyoypkmp). The sibling modules are included at their fixed flat paths, so the handler compiles against them; the test then observes their effects at the verb's boundary: the base is the identity map of the owned set, the key is a fresh handle no other record holds (two drafts, two distinct handles), the registry entry is `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, and the workspace is a real jj workspace at the derived path. Their internal contracts — the mint, the digest algorithm, the registry's read/write/scan and the workspace seam's calls — belong to the gates that own them (rkmqmuzx, pxmmonpz, ttzpnuml, ztzpqrrr).

The no-printing rule (utrzvyyt). The handler returns its lines and the envelope writes them, so the module prints nothing: the check runs the handler in a child process — this same test binary, filtered to the probe and put in child mode — twice, once stopping before the call and once after it, and requires the two stdout and stderr streams to be byte-for-byte equal; any line the call printed is exactly the difference, on either stream. A test cannot read its own stdout with `std` alone, so the child process is how the stream is observed; the probe names no print macro, so a comment that mentions one does not trip it, and it catches output written anywhere on the call's path.

What this gate leaves out, deliberately: the handle's format and minting, the identity algorithm and base construction, the registry's storage, schema and discovery, the jj workspace seam's path, add, forget and list, the record's loading and validation (qorqswry), the literal per-user root location (no recorded prerequisite fixes it), the exact text and separator of the lines beyond naming the handle and the path (the no-printing check fixes that the handler writes none of them), the refusal's rendering and exit status, how a node id is resolved, and what a call does when a named id names nothing. The check names no function inside the module and no wording of the decision, so a rewording that keeps what xulmunov decides leaves it intact.

The linked-workspace use (mrwtusss, zttrwlts). The registry and the namespace are the repository's, not the invocation workspace's. The test makes a scratch repository with `jj git init`, adds a second working copy with `jj workspace add`, and drives the handler from that linked workspace: the record the call opens is read from the trunk working copy's `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, while the linked workspace's own `.deccy/work/` holds no record for it, because the registry is one for the repository. It then opens one draft from the trunk and one from the linked workspace of the same repository and requires the two records' workspace paths to carry the same namespace directory: the derivation follows the repository's root, so the linked path cannot pick a different namespace. The same call in the linked workspace returns its lines rather than an `Err` — opening a draft writes no graph state and is not bracketed (ooquotol), so the trunk-only door mrwtusss fixes for graph-writing verbs stays off this verb and the verb keeps working outside the trunk. The check reads only the registry directories and the recorded paths; it names no accessor, no namespace spelling and no trunk-detection mechanism.

The matrix cells: the code-to-code cell is `test`. The edges from inline prose and EARS prerequisites into this code dependent land in natural-to-code (fidelity) and structured-to-code (conformance), and the plan fixes one runnable test for the whole licence; the test reads the behaviour those commitments require of the implementation rather than reviewing prose, and those cells are flagged for a matrix entry.
